title: James Ball
gist: An author index page (not an article) for James Ball, political editor at the New World; his 11 listed Prospect pieces map a tech-and-institutions beat — the metaverse's death, distrust of the data driving government, whether Five Eyes survives the Signal scandal, breaking up Big Tech, and a week inside container-ship supply chains.

insights.claim: The metaverse is written about as something already at its end, a reporter's post-mortem framing rather than a forecast, marking how quickly the 2021-era immersive-computing narrative collapsed.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: A worked example of a platform narrative dying without a formal failure event — a template for assessing current AI-hype durability.
insights.quote: Life at the end of the metaverse
insights.locator: Technology / Life at the end of the metaverse

insights.claim: The same writer publishes a prescriptive case for cutting Big Tech down to size, indicating that structural remedies rather than conduct fixes are the framing in mainstream UK ideas media.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Break-up framing in elite UK commentary keeps structural-remedy risk alive for platform valuations even where enforcement lags.
insights.quote: How to cut Big Tech down to size
insights.locator: Technology / How to cut Big Tech down to size

insights.claim: A dedicated piece argues the data driving government cannot be trusted, targeting official statistics as the weak link in policymaking rather than the policies themselves.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: If official data quality is degrading, macro releases carry more revision risk and policy reaction functions become less predictable.
insights.quote: Why the data driving government can’t be trusted
insights.locator: Data / Why the data driving government can’t be trusted

insights.claim: The survival of the Five Eyes intelligence alliance is treated as an open question following the Signal scandal, framing allied intelligence-sharing as contingent rather than permanent.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Intelligence-sharing fragmentation among Anglophone allies would reshape defence procurement and sovereign-capability spending.
insights.quote: Can Five Eyes survive the Signal scandal?
insights.locator: United States / Can Five Eyes survive the Signal scandal?

insights.claim: Academic freedom is covered as an active assault rather than a debate, and a piece asks whether the pandemic killed God — both framing institutional legitimacy as the underlying subject.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Political interference in universities is a funding and reputational risk factor for the higher-education sector.
insights.locator: Free Speech / The assault on academic freedom

insights.claim: The writer spent a week aboard a container ship to report the supply chain from the inside, an on-the-ground reporting method applied to global logistics rather than desk analysis.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Primary-source shipping reporting is a useful independent read on freight conditions versus index data.
insights.quote: Inside the supply chain: my week on a container ship

insights.claim: The same author asked whether CNN has sold out and argued Britain must prepare in advance for a great wave of Hong Kong immigrants, pairing media-ownership critique with anticipatory migration policy.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Anticipated migration surges drive UK housing, services and local-authority funding pressure well before they appear in official flows.
insights.quote: Hong Kong: Britain must prepare now for a great wave of immigrants
insights.locator: Politics / Hong Kong: Britain must prepare now
